messages:
Rina: Quick UX question for autofallback: should the platform require a human unlock before traffic is routed back to the primary model, or should it auto-return after a stability window?
Carlos: prefer auto-return but gated by an SLO check: only reenable if 5xx < 0.5% and p95 latency < baseline + 20%. Otherwise keep in fallback.
Tess: That makes sense. From a compliance POV we also need an append-only audit row for each state transition (trigger -> fallback -> resume). CSV exportable.
Devon: We should add a severity field to the incident so paging rules differ. Eg severity=high pages oncall immediately and disables auto-reenable until manual ack. Low severity follows auto-reenable path.
Rina: Good call. So incident flow idea: 1) autofallback fires -> create incident with {severity, trigger_type, affected_routes}. 2) send console inbox + optional page if severity high. 3) In inbox actions: [Acknowledge], [Hold until resumed], [Open rollback]. If no ack and severity low, wait stability_window then auto-return.
Carlos: UX detail: show a tiny cost preview: delta_per_minute and estimate hourly impact if left in fallback. PMs care about that.
Tess: Also add model-compatibility reason: e.g., "fallback target uses 4-bit quantized weights, lacks some tokenizers" so engineers know potential quality regressions.
Devon: Ops infra note: add a debounce on incident creation per route+window so we don't generate thousands of incidents during a flapping period. One rolling incident is enough.
infra-bot: I can consolidate incidents and attach a summary. Will include counts by trigger, earliest_ts, latest_ts, and attach up to 10 scrubbed samples.
Rina: For audit, we need fields: incident_id, event_ts, actor (system/human), action, previous_config, new_config, rationale. All immutable.
Carlos: Suggest CSV header: incident_id,event_ts,actor,action,prev_cfg,new_cfg,rationale
Tess: For the console timeline view, add filters for severity, trigger, model and a quick "why" expand that shows the decision path (thresholds and matching policy).
Devon: Telemetry: tag requests served during fallback with fallback_id and fallback_label so downstream analytics can attribute. Also record token_cost and model_variant.
Rina: Example operator inbox payload sketch for API:
```json
{
  "incident_id": "fb-2026-03-22-77",
  "severity": "low",
  "trigger": "p95_latency>500ms",
  "fallback_target": "gpt-small-4bit",
  "actions": ["ack", "hold_until_resumed", "rollback"],
  "auto_reenable_after": 900
}
```
Carlos: Note auto_reenable_after should be env-configurable and also SLO-aware (ignore timer if SLO conditions unmet).
Tess: Add a postmortem bundle action in the UI that packages: incident CSV + 10 samples + traces + cost delta snapshot. One-click export.
Devon: RBAC: only users with release or ops role can click hold/rollback in prod. Staging can be looser. Enforce on API.
infra-bot: Will apply RBAC guard and rate-limit ack/hold calls to 1 per minute per incident to avoid scripts flipping things.
Rina: Also consider an "auto-rollback" policy: if quality detectors (synthetic evals or user-quality signals) show regression > threshold during fallback, platform should optionally revert to previous config automatically. That should be opt-in.
Carlos: Good idea. Put it behind a policy flag: auto_rollback_on_quality_loss. If enabled, require a second approver to disable.
Tess: For transparency, add a public incident link that opens a read-only view with the CSV snapshot and timeline so cross-functional teams can review without changing state.
Devon: Testing: plan a staging run next Friday to simulate p95 spike and 5xx burst. We'll verify inbox generation, RBAC, CSV export, and the stability gating for auto-return.
Rina: I'll mock the inbox UI and a timeline wireframe. Will include the cost delta widget and the "explain why" panel.
Carlos: Send the mock to #design-review when ready. Happy to review.
infra-bot: Logged event fb-2026-03-22-77 created by auto-controller. Link: telemetry://fallback/fb-2026-03-22-77
Tess: One last UX wording check: button label "Hold until resumed" vs "Pause auto-resume". I vote for "Hold until resumed".
Rina: Agreed. Thanks all, I'll post the mock later this week.
Devon: I'll schedule the staging sim and add signal slices for telemetry.
Tess: I'll draft the CSV schema for audit compliance. End thread.
